artifact: T2-5 landmine catalogue as executable eval cases
generated_by: tests/test_landmines.py (offline, deterministic, no network / no LLM)
bar: a landmine passes when the pipeline never fakes a pass: the correct outcome is an honest status (reserved / missing / incorporated_by_reference / partial+needs_review), never a fabricated body.

landmines.behaviour: '[Reserved]' -> reserved; item omitted entirely -> reserved (absence of an abolished item is not a failure); pre-2021 'Selected Financial Data' body -> substantive pass.

landmines.source: Item 9C (HFCAA) and Item 16 (Form 10-K Summary) are conditional/optional
landmines.behaviour: present -> source-exact pass; absent -> honest 'missing' with empty span (tri-state scorer maps not-TOC-listed missing to null, not a real omission).

landmines.source: combined heading (same shape as existing 'Items 1 and 2')
landmines.behaviour: both 7 and 7A -> partial, share one span, both carry a 'combined' warning.
resolver._collect_10k collects 10-K + 10-K/A, rejects 10-Q / 8-K / NT 10-K; amendment flagged is_amendment. No exact-match trap in our fetcher.

landmines.source: TOC must be excluded before anchoring, not only compared after
landmines.note: assess_toc is post-hoc (marks toc_rejected only when a later body duplicate exists). For a TOC-only item with NO body, a SECOND mechanism catches it: boundary document-order enforcement drops the TOC candidate (start < prev_start), so the item comes back 'missing' with an empty span, never the dotted TOC line as content. Candidate is never silently dropped — it keeps its toc_reasons.
landmines.behaviour: Item listed only in anchored TOC -> missing, empty span, TOC line not leaked.

landmines.source: Part III may incorporate by reference to DEF 14A (proxy)
landmines.behaviour: Item 10/11 pointing to the proxy -> incorporated_by_reference (not a faked pass). Fetching the DEF 14A and the 120-day rule is a documented network step, out of the offline pipeline's scope.

landmines.source: edgartools GitHub issue #454 — Part I/II item-number collision, 'Item 1' returns the wrong section
landmines.behaviour: canonical-code + document-order resolver keeps the real Part I Item 1 body and rejects a later stray 'Item 1.' running header. We do not reproduce edgartools' collision.

landmines.source: 10-K bundled with a glossy annual report (EX-13); wrapper 10-K binds a Financial Section after the last item
landmines.behaviour: main-doc scorer picks the 10-K over the LARGER EX-13 annual report (exhibit penalty); terminal item's span is cut at the appended 'FINANCIAL SECTION' break instead of swallowing ~30K chars.

landmines.source: Intel / Citi class: main document is a page-range index into a bound annual report
landmines.behaviour: filing_class=cross_reference_index; each item -> incorporated_by_reference pointer, provenance=cross_reference_pointer, needs_review=True, empty sha (never a fabricated body).

landmines.source: edgartools chunks filings past a ~50MB threshold; offsets can drift across chunk boundaries
landmines.behaviour: pipeline normalises the whole document once (no chunking), so every span stays a provable source-exact span (sha256 + raw round-trip) regardless of size. Verified on a ~1.2MB doc; the property is size-independent.
